anatomy.lede: A broad, flat head with eyes and mouth pointing upwards: the whitemargin stargazer is built to wait under the sand.

hotspots.label: Upward-facing eye
hotspots.text: The eyes sit on top of the head, the feature that gives the family its name. Buried, the fish leaves little but its eyes showing.

hotspots.label: Upturned mouth
hotspots.text: The fringe of small fleshy cirri along the edge of the mouth keeps sand out while the buried fish breathes. Inside is a lure that draws prey within striking range.

hotspots.label: Shoulder spine
hotspots.text: Behind the gill cover and above the pectoral fin sits a venomous cleithral spine, one on each side.

hotspots.label: Black first dorsal fin
hotspots.text: The black first dorsal fin, with four spines, is one of the marks that identify this species.

survival.lede: The stargazer hunts and hides in the same way: by staying buried and still.

tactics.title: Ambush from below
tactics.text: Stargazers bury themselves in sand and then leap up to seize fish and invertebrates passing overhead.

tactics.title: Hidden in plain sight
tactics.text: This species spends most of its time buried in sand or mud, which is why it is so rarely seen.

tactics.title: Two venomous spines
tactics.text: Stargazers carry two large venomous spines behind the gill covers, above the pectoral fins.

threats.title: Fishing
threats.text: FishBase rates this species as moderately vulnerable to fishing. Its status is Least Concern, last assessed in 2023.
